question: to the Commission Kathleen Van Brempt (S&D) Subject:

Under Council Regulation (EU) 2026/382, from 1 July 2026 until 1 July 2028 a customs duty of EUR 3 is applicable per tariff sub-heading in consignments whose intrinsic value does not exceed a total of EUR 150. The objectives of fairer competition and improved customs controls are justified. However, there are indications that the levy per tariff sub-heading is making mixed orders disproportionately expensive. In one of the reported cases, an order for electronic components worth EUR 26.81 incurred EUR 14.52 in additional customs charges. This may affect hobbyists, repairers, researchers and small businesses, particularly where specialised components are concerned and which are not available within the EU. 1.

Is the Commission aware of the potentially disproportionate impact of the levy per tariff sub-heading, and does it intend to examine the impact on consumers, looking, amongst other things, at the relationship between the levy and the intrinsic value of consignments?

Is the Commission considering applying targeted adjustments, such as a maximum amount per consignment, a minimum threshold or a broader grouping of closely related tariff sub-headings, with appropriate safeguards to prevent circumvention?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (7.9.2026) The Commission underlines that the temporary EUR 3 customs duty is intended as a transitional solution until the EU Customs Data Hub for e-commerce becomes operational on 1 July 2028, at which point customs duties will be calculated based on the product’s tariff classification, origin and value. The EUR 3 customs duty is applied per declaration line (item) irrespective of the quantity, as every customs duty is today applied per item. The Guidance on implementation of the EUR 3 duty1 provides several examples on how to declare goods. The Commission has further clarified2 that economic operators must be encouraged to use one declaration line per goods sharing tariff classification in H7. It is currently not envisaged to apply any changes or adjustments. Goods can benefit from reduced or zero duty in case of preferential trade and customs EU agreements3. Regarding the ‘customs charges’, consumers buying online are not legally responsible for paying the EUR 3 customs duty to the customs authorities. The debtor is the platform or seller or any other business involved in the sale and transport of the imported goods; it can be the carrier or any authorised representative. The business decision of charging the EUR 3 duty and additional charges to consumers stays with the relevant sellers/platforms. As concerns the impact of the measure, the Commission will have to assess, by 1 October 20264 whether a diversion of trade flows occurs following the introduction of the temporary EUR 3 duty and, if needed, whether to extend the scope of the EUR 3 to all items in consignments not exceeding EUR 150.
